newsitem.title: SPAIN: SOCCER-PIZZI TAKES OVER FROM RONALDO.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-PIZZI TAKES OVER FROM RONALDO.

text.p: Spain international Juan Pizzi will deputise for Brazilian striker Ronaldo on Sunday as Barcelona resume their challenge for the Spanish title.

Barcelona, who meet struggling Hercules, are only two points behind Real Madrid, who must be haunted by the memory of seeing similar leads slip away in the last three matches of both the 1991-92 and 1992-93 seasons.
Real's decline in recent games has coincided with a run of good form for Barcelona.
The Catalans have already taken the European Cup Winners' Cup and are still in the running to grab the domestic league and Cup competitions and with them an unprecedented triple.

Ronaldo, who announced his departure from Barcelona this week, scored the winning goals in the Cup Winners' Cup final and in the league matches against Real and third-placed Deportivo Coruna that have put Barcelona back into contention for the title.
He will miss Sunday's game and the rest of the season because of international duty but the strength in depth of the Barcelona squad gives Pizzi his chance.
Pizzi was the leading goalscorer in Spain last season and is a regular in the country's national side.
The problems surrounding Ronaldo must have unnerved even Barcelona's seasoned professionals.
"Less Ronaldo and more Hercules," commented deputy club captain Josep Guardiola.
"For a long time we've been going on about renovations, contracts...let's talk about football."
Guardiola's own presence at Barcelona next season is still in doubt.
The former Olympic gold medallist has been widely linked with several Italian clubs, and could yet resume his partnership with Ronaldo, who seems likely to move to Inter Milan.
Some speculation has even linked Ronaldo with Real Madrid, where club president Lorenzo Sanz is gloating at the discomfort of his Barcelona counterparts.
"They're making fools of themselves," said Sanz.
Sanz's side also face a side struggling against relegation in newly-promoted Extremadura.
Real will welcome back strikers Davor Suker and Predrag Mijatovic from suspension but will be without set-piece ace Roberto Carlos, who is also with the Brazilian national side.
